newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice market cheered by Philippines sale news.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice market cheered by Philippines sale news.

text.p: The Thai rice market rolled out of the doldrums on news that the Philippines was to buy 205,000 tonnes of local rice, trade sources said on Thursday.
But otherwise, activities in the market were limited mostly to covering obligations as buyers of high-quality rice remained sidelined by high prices.
Thai Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn announced on his return from a visit to the Philippines that Manila had agreed to buy 205,000 tonnes of 25 percent grade rice from Thailand.
The deal would be on a government-to-government basis, he said, but did not provide price details.

The price of Thai benchmark 100 percent B grade was quoted around $370-390 per tonne FOB Bangkok compared with $380-400 per tonnes last week and fragrant 100 percent grade rice was unchanged at $620-630 per tonnes.

But the price of broken rice jumped on rising demand as exporters needed the rice for blending in order to produce lower grade quality such as 15 percent grade now being shipped to Indonesia in large quantities.
At least six vessels were loading 26,300 tonnes of 15-25 percent rice for shipment to that country. The broken rice was quoted around $225-230 per tonne compared with $220 last week.
"The price of broken rice is likely to rise further with the Manila's order of 25 percent grade," one trader said.
The market gave a cold shoulder to the forecast on 1996/97 (April-March) rice output, saying 21.27 million tonnes are in line with the market expectation.
At ports, vessels were loading around 86,000 tonnes of rice for shipments to Indonesia, Japan, Iran, Hong Kong, Brunei, China and Singapore.
Thailand exported 339,421 tonnes of rice between January 1-28 compared with 511,702 during the same period in 1996.
